items.prompt: In the past 4 weeks, how much of the time did your asthma keep you from getting as much done at work, school or at home?
items.scale_hint: 1 = all of the time, 2 = most of the time, 3 = some of the time, 4 = a little of the time, 5 = none of the time

items.prompt: During the past 4 weeks, how often have you had shortness of breath?
items.scale_hint: 1 = more than once a day, 2 = once a day, 3 = three to six times a week, 4 = once or twice a week, 5 = not at all

items.prompt: During the past 4 weeks, how often did your asthma symptoms wake you up at night or earlier than usual in the morning?
items.scale_hint: 1 = four or more nights a week, 2 = two or three nights a week, 3 = once a week, 4 = once or twice in the four weeks, 5 = not at all

items.prompt: During the past 4 weeks, how often have you used your rescue inhaler or nebulizer medication?
items.scale_hint: 1 = three or more times per day, 2 = one or two times per day, 3 = two or three times per week, 4 = once a week or less, 5 = not at all

items.prompt: How would you rate your asthma control during the past 4 weeks?
items.scale_hint: 1 = not controlled at all, 2 = poorly controlled, 3 = somewhat controlled, 4 = well controlled, 5 = completely controlled

risk_questions.prompt: In the last twelve months, how many times have you needed a course of steroid tablets for your asthma?
Roughly how many rescue inhaler canisters have you gone through in the last year?
Have you ever been admitted to hospital or intensive care because of your asthma?

controlled.summary: Well controlled on current therapy. Continue as-needed ICS-formoterol reliever therapy; reinforce technique and adherence; no step-up indicated.
controlled.patient_goal: Keep your asthma as settled as it is now, and keep your reliever use low.

medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs twice daily, plus 1 puff as needed for symptoms (max 12 puffs/day)

partial.summary: Not well controlled. Step up to low-dose ICS-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) after confirming inhaler technique and adherence.
partial.patient_goal: Get to the point where asthma is not waking you at night or limiting your day.

medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs twice daily, plus 1 puff as needed for symptoms (max 12 puffs/day)
Inhale 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath or wheeze

poor.summary: Poorly controlled. Step up to medium-dose ICS-formoterol MART with a short oral corticosteroid course to regain control, review technique, adherence and trigger exposure, and arrange earlier clinical review.
poor.patient_goal: Bring symptoms down so you can sleep through the night and get through a normal day.

medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs twice daily, plus 1 puff as needed for symptoms (max 12 puffs/day)
Inhale 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath or wheeze
Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily for 5 days

very-poor.summary: Very poorly controlled. Medium-dose ICS-formoterol MART plus a short oral corticosteroid course, urgent clinician contact, and respiratory specialist referral.
very-poor.patient_goal: Get your breathing stable quickly and have a clinician review you within the next few days.

medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs twice daily, plus 1 puff as needed for symptoms (max 12 puffs/day)
Inhale 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath or wheeze
Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily for 5 days

emergency_rules: Red flags of a severe attack happening NOW: can only speak a few words at a time, breathless at rest, reliever not helping or needed every 1-2 hours, chest pain with breathlessness, blue lips or fingertips, drowsiness or confusion. If you hear any of these, stop the questionnaire and say ONCE: "This sounds like it could be an emergency. Please hang up, use your reliever, and call 911 right now." Then end the call — do not continue the questions.

experts.name: Respiratory physician
experts.system_prompt: You are a consultant respiratory physician reviewing an automatically drafted asthma plan before a human clinician sees it. Judge whether the step-up choice matches the ACT band and reported risk factors under current GINA-style stepwise care. Be concise and specific. Return JSON only.

experts.name: Clinical pharmacist
experts.system_prompt: You are a clinical pharmacist reviewing a drafted asthma regimen. Check dose, device, duplicate therapy, PRN limits, quantity and refills for internal consistency and practicality. Return JSON only.

experts.name: Medication safety reviewer
experts.system_prompt: You are a medication safety reviewer. Your only job is to flag anything that could harm this patient: allergy conflicts, contraindications, overlapping beta-agonists, oral steroid risk, or an under-treated high-risk phenotype. Raise "concern" if there is any real safety issue. Return JSON only.
